subject: SLA carveout and maintenance cadence — ClearBank counteroffer
messages:
From: Tim Jensen <tim.jensen@clearbank.com>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: claire.lambert@clearbank.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA concerns — maintenance windows & credits

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the demo last week — ClearBank's infra team raised two items on the SLA and maintenance language that we need to surface before procurement will sign:

1) Maintenance windows — ClearBank is highly regulated and cannot accept routine maintenance between 07:00-19:00 ET. We need scheduled maintenance confined to a 02:00-06:00 ET window (and a maximum 4-hour window per event).
2) Service credits — request a clearer staircase for uptime below 99.99, and a minimum floor (we propose 99.95 as the baseline with credits increasing at 0.1% decrements).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to tighter blackout windows and the proposed credit formula? I attached a short PDF with our compliance team's ask.

Thanks,
Tim Jensen
Director, Infrastructure Security
ClearBank
Attachment: ClearBank_SLA_Request.pdf (PDF, 245 KB)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Jensen <tim.jensen@clearbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA concerns — maintenance windows & credits

Hi Tim — appreciate the clear ask and the PDF.

Short answer: we can get most of the way there but need to confirm a couple of operational tradeoffs with ops and legal. Two quick points up front:
- We can restrict routine maintenance to a narrow overnight window on a per-region basis, but some global upgrades require staggered windows; we can commit to a maximum 4-hour scheduled window per event and 72 hours' notice for non-emergent changes.
- For credits, Marissa (cc'd) will propose language that maps to a credit staircase; I expect Redwood to accept a 99.95 floor for the Order Form with a clarified credit calculation rather than the 99.99 absolute floor you proposed.

I'm attaching our initial counterproposal (tracked redlines) for the MSA + Order Form; Marissa will highlight any legal carveouts (emergency maintenance, security patches, and force majeure).

Next step: Marissa, can you draft the legal redline we discussed and flag any operational exceptions for Connor? Aditya — can you own the procurement routing once Claire confirms?

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redline_suggestion.docx (DOCX, 85 KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: Draft redlines — ClearBank MSA & Order Form (SLA/support)

Team — attaching tracked changes for the MSA + Order Form focusing on the SLA/support section. Key legal positions below (high level):

- Uptime: propose Order Form commitment of 99.95% monthly uptime for the production service in the primary region. We will not accept a hard 99.99% guarantee without a separate Dedicated commitment (higher tier).

- Credits: implement a staircase that pays credits as a percentage of monthly service fees: 99.95–99.0 => 10%; 99.0–97.5 => 25%; <97.5 => 50%. Credits capped at 100% of monthly fees for the affected service. We documented calculation examples in Appendix A.

- Response times: P1 acknowledged within 15 minutes, P1 remediation target 4 hours for infrastructure incidents; P2 acknowledged within 1 hour, remediation best-effort but within 48 hours for software issues.

- Maintenance windows: schedule routine maintenance in a 02:00–06:00 ET window where possible; for global upgrades require staggered regional windows and prior notice not less than 72 hours. Emergency maintenance (security/patch) is excluded from scheduled notice but will have immediate customer notification and post-event RCA.

- Exceptions & Audit: provide SOC2 evidence and an operations runbook as part of onboarding; include a single escalation path to Redwood's Ops Director + named support contacts for ClearBank.

I attached the track-changes file. Connor: please add operational caps (max duration per event) and confirm rollback/mitigation language. Rachel/Aditya: once we align, I'll prepare a clean counterproposal PDF for Tim/Claire and a DocuSign packet for procurement.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Legal — Redwood Inference
Attachment: redlines_MSA_orderform_track_changes.docx (DOCX, 167 KB)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Jensen <tim.jensen@clearbank.com>, Claire Lambert <claire.lambert@clearbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 16:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA concerns — maintenance windows & credits

Tim / Claire — thanks for the patience while we looped ops and legal. Below is a concise summary of Redwood's counterproposal to address ClearBank's compliance concerns. The attached PDF is the clean Order Form with the SLA section called out.

Summary of counterproposal (high level):
- Uptime: 99.95% monthly in the primary region (we can discuss a higher commitment under a Dedicated capacity addendum).
- Credit staircase: 99.95–99.0 => 10% credit; 99.0–97.5 => 25%; <97.5 => 50%; credit capped at 100% of monthly subscription for the impacted service. Exact formulas/examples in the attached.
- Maintenance: routine maintenance scheduled to 02:00–06:00 ET (max 4 hours/event) with 72 hours' advance notice for non-emergencies. Global upgrades may be staggered; we'll provide region-by-region times at least 72 hours prior.
- Emergency maintenance: immediate notification required; no prior notice but post-event RCA and mitigation plan within 5 business days.
- Response & escalation: P1 ack within 15 minutes, P1 remediation target 4 hours; named Ops director escalation for ClearBank.

Next steps:
1) Marissa will send the official redline packet (attached).
2) If ClearBank agrees to the Order Form language, I'll send a DocuSign link to procurement for signature.

Link to counterproposal + signing: https://app.docusign.com/embeddedSigning/abcdef123456

Attachment: Counterproposal_OrderForm.pdf (PDF, 132 KB)

Best regards,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Tim Jensen <tim.jensen@clearbank.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@clearbank.com, claire.lambert@clearbank.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA concerns — maintenance windows & credits

Rachel — thanks, that summary helps. Procurement will review the clean Order Form and the credit staircase. I am looping procurement@clearbank.com to pick up DocuSign and run internal approvals. We may come back with one narrow final redline on the emergency maintenance notification SLA but that's procedural rather than substantive.

I'll aim to get procurement's input by EOD Monday. In the meantime, please send the procurement packet (we require a completed procurement_form.pdf attached).

Regards,
Tim
Attachment: procurement_form.pdf (PDF, 64 KB)
